akhfash:6-6.t: He said ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرْ﴾: jussive (majzūm) because it is the answer to the prohibition. Some read it in the nominative, ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾, meaning "seeking increase" (مستكثرا), and that is the better of the two meanings. «[Translator's note: the nominative تَسْتَكْثِرُ is the reading of the standard text; the jussive is a variant reading.]»

akhfash:16-16.t: And He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهُ كان لآيَاتِنَا عَنِيداً﴾, that is: obstinate (معاندا).

akhfash:33-33.t: And He said ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ﴾; and "دَبَرَ" has the meaning of "أَدْبَرَ" ("to turn away"). They say "قَبَّحَ اللهُ ما قَبَلَ مِنْهُ وما دَبَر" ("may Allah make hideous what came of it and what went"), and they said "عامٌ قَابِلٌ" ("the coming year") and did not say "مُقْبِلٌ".

akhfash:35-36.t: And He said ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ﴾ ﴿نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾: ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ is accusative because it is a khabar (predicate) to ﴿إِحْدَى الكُبَر﴾; ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ is accusative because it is a predicate to a definite noun and the sentence was already complete before it (silence there being acceptable), so it became a ḥāl (circumstantial); and it (the feminine referent) is "the warner" — just as you say "إِنَّهُ لَعَبْدُ اللهِ قَائِماً" ("he is indeed ʿAbdullāh, standing"). And some said: "it is only" "قُمْ نَذِيراً فَأَنْذِر" ("arise as a warner and warn"). «[Translator's note: i.e., they link نَذِيرًا to the command at the opening of the sura, «قُمْ فَأَنْذِرْ» (74:2).]»

akhfash:54-54.t: And He said ﴿كَلاَّ إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾, that is: the Qur'an is a reminder.

daas-irab:1-7.t:
﴿يا أَيُّهَا﴾ a vocative particle, and the one addressed (munādā), indeclinable (mabnī) on ḍamma, in the position of an accusative (manṣūb), and hā is a particle of alerting (tanbīh); and ﴿الْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾ badal (substitute) of أيّ; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿قُمْ﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir). ﴿فَأَنْذِرْ﴾ an imperative verb conjoined (maʿṭūf) to قم; the clause قم is also initial, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَرَبَّكَ﴾ a fronted mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿فَكَبِّرْ﴾ the fāʾ occurring in the apodosis of an omitted condition, and an imperative verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَثِيابَكَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and a fronted mafʿūl bihi. ﴿فَطَهِّرْ﴾ parsed like فكبر. ﴿وَالرُّجْزَ فَاهْجُرْ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَلا تَمْنُنْ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and an imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by the prohibitive lā; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
﴿وَلِرَبِّكَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them. ﴿فَاصْبِرْ﴾ the i'rab of its like has preceded.

daas-irab:8-10.t: ﴿فَإِذا﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle. ﴿إذا﴾ a conditional adverb of time that does not make jussive. ﴿نُقِرَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿فِي النَّاقُورِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿فَذلِكَ﴾ the fāʾ is connective (rābiṭa), and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ badal (substitute) of the demonstrative; and ﴿يَوْمٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿عَسِيرٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ) of a condition, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَلَى الْكافِرِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to عسير; and ﴿غَيْرُ﴾ a second adjective of يوم; and ﴿يَسِيرٍ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct).

daas-irab:11-12.t: ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ an imperative verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and the nūn is for protection (nūn al-wiqāya), and the yāʾ of the first person is mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَمَنْ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the yāʾ of the first person; and ﴿خَلَقْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil. ﴿وَحِيداً﴾ ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is the ṣila (relative clause), with no grammatical position. ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb, and they stand in the place of the second object; and ﴿مالًا﴾ its first mafʿūl bihi. ﴿مَمْدُوداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it.

daas-irab:13-15.t: ﴿وَبَنِينَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to مالا; and ﴿شُهُوداً﴾ an adjective (ṣifa). ﴿وَمَهَّدْتُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿لَهُ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb; and ﴿تَمْهِيداً﴾ mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿ثُمَّ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿يَطْمَعُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿أَنْ أَزِيدَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, whose fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by removal of the preposition (manṣūb bi-nazʿ al-khāfiḍ).

daas-irab:16-17.t: ﴿كَلَّا إِنَّهُ﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr), and inna and its noun; and ﴿كانَ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) past verb whose noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿لِآياتِنا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what follows them; and ﴿عَنِيداً﴾ khabar (predicate) of kāna; the verbal clause is the khabar of inna, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent, and the hāʾ is first mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿صَعُوداً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:18-23.t: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ﴾ inna and its noun, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is the khabar (predicate) of إنه, and the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl). ﴿وَقَدَّرَ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to فكر; and ﴿فَقُتِلَ﴾ a passive past verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; and ﴿كَيْفَ﴾ an interrogative noun as ḥāl (circumstantial); the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿قَدَّرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and the verses that follow are conjoined to it, up to verse 23.

daas-irab:24-25.t: ﴿فَقالَ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction, and a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿إِنْ هذا﴾ in is negative, and the demonstrative is mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿سِحْرٌ﴾ khabar (predicate); the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿يُؤْثَرُ﴾ a passive imperfect verb, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent; the clause is an adjective (ṣifa) of سحر; and ﴿إِنْ﴾ negative; and ﴿هذا﴾ the demonstrative as mubtadaʾ; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿قَوْلُ الْبَشَرِ﴾ khabar, annexed to البشر; the clause is an emphasis (taʾkīd) of the preceding one.

daas-irab:26-30.t: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ﴾ the sīn of futurity, and an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿سَقَرَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is badal (substitute) of سأرهقه. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle; and ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿أَدْراكَ﴾ a past verb and its first mafʿūl bihi, and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿ما سَقَرُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar; the clause stands in place of the second object of أدراك; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿تُبْقِي﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) clause; and ﴿لا تَذَرُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ﴾ khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ; and ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; the clause is a second ḥāl; and ﴿عَلَيْها﴾ a fronted khabar; and ﴿تِسْعَةَ﴾ part of a number, indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa, in the position of a nominative (marfūʿ) as a postponed mubtadaʾ; and ﴿عَشَرَ﴾ part of a number, indeclinable on fatḥa, with no grammatical position. The clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:31-31.t: ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿ما﴾ negative; and ﴿جَعَلْنا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); and ﴿أَصْحابَ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi (direct object), annexed to ﴿النَّارِ﴾; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction (ḥaṣr); and ﴿مَلائِكَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿عِدَّتَهُمْ﴾ first mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿فِتْنَةً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi, with an omitted muḍāf, its implied form being «a cause of trial» (سبب فتنة); and ﴿لِلَّذِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) what precedes them; and ﴿كَفَرُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause). And ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an implied an after the lām of purpose (taʿlīl); the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to the second جعلنا; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent); and ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَزْدادَ﴾ conjoined to ليستيقن; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿آمَنُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the ṣila of الذين; and ﴿إِيماناً﴾ mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ﴾ the wāw is a conjunction, and ﴿لا﴾ negative, and an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿أُوتُوا﴾ a passive past verb, and the wāw is the nāʾib fāʿil; and ﴿الْكِتابَ﴾ second mafʿūl bihi. ﴿وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ conjoined to الذين; the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَلِيَقُولَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative by an implied an after the lām of purpose; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is in the position of a genitive by the lām, and the preposition with its genitive noun are conjoined to «ليستيقن..»; and ﴿الَّذِينَ﴾ fāʿil; and ﴿فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ﴾ a fronted khabar (predicate); and ﴿مَرَضٌ﴾ a postponed mubtadaʾ (subject); the nominal clause is the ṣila of الذين. ﴿وَالْكافِرُونَ﴾ conjoined to الذين; and ﴿ماذا﴾ an interrogative noun, a fronted mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿أَرادَ اللَّهُ﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil; the clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl); and ﴿بِهذا﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; and ﴿مَثَلًا﴾: ḥāl (circumstantial). And ﴿كَذلِكَ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa) of an omitted mafʿūl muṭlaq (absolute object); and ﴿يُضِلُّ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; and ﴿مَنْ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿يَشاءُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); the clause is the ṣila. ﴿وَيَهْدِي مَنْ يَشاءُ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle and mā is negative; and ﴿يَعْلَمُ جُنُودَ رَبِّكَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi, annexed to ربك; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿هُوَ﴾ fāʿil of يعلم; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿وَ﴾ the wāw is a resumptive particle. ﴿وَما﴾ the wāw is resumptive and mā is negative; and ﴿هِيَ﴾ mubtadaʾ; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of restriction; and ﴿ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ khabar, to which the preposition and its genitive noun after it are attached; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:32-37.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr). ﴿وَالْقَمَرِ﴾ the wāw is a particle of oath and a preposition, and a preposition and its genitive noun attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted verb of oath. ﴿وَاللَّيْلِ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it; and ﴿إِذْ﴾ an adverb for past time; and ﴿أَدْبَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); the clause is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by annexation. ﴿وَالصُّبْحِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿إِذا﴾ an adverb of time; and ﴿أَسْفَرَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is in the position of a genitive by annexation; and ﴿إِنَّها لَإِحْدَى﴾ inna and its noun, and the shifted lām (al-lām al-muzaḥlaqa); and ﴿إحدى الْكُبَرِ﴾ khabar (predicate) of inna, annexed to الكبر; the nominal clause is the response to the oath (jawāb al-qasam), with no grammatical position. And ﴿نَذِيراً﴾ tamyīz (specification); and ﴿لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to نذيرا; and ﴿لِمَنْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, badal (substitute) of His words للبشر; and ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿مِنْكُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause); and ﴿أَنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the fāʿil is latent; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is mafʿūl bihi (direct object). ﴿أَوْ﴾ a conjunction; and ﴿يَتَأَخَّرَ﴾ conjoined to يتقدم.

daas-irab:38-42.t: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ﴾ mubtadaʾ (subject), annexed to نفس; and ﴿بِما﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) كسبت; and ﴿كَسَبَتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿رَهِينَةٌ﴾ khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the verbal clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of ما, and the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. And ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; and ﴿أَصْحابَ الْيَمِينِ﴾ excepted (mustathnā) by illā, annexed to اليمين; and ﴿فِي جَنَّاتٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to an omitted ḥāl (circumstantial); and ﴿يَتَساءَلُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَنِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to what precedes them; and ﴿ما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ; and ﴿سَلَكَكُمْ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the verbal clause is the khabar of the mubtadaʾ; and ﴿فِي سَقَرَ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the nominal clause is the object of an omitted saying (maqūl li-qawl maḥdhūf).

daas-irab:43-47.t: ﴿قالُوا﴾ a past verb and its fāʿil (agent); the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿لَمْ نَكُ﴾ a defective (nāqiṣ) imperfect verb in the jussive (majzūm) by lam, the sign of its jussive being the sukūn on the nūn, which is dropped for lightness, and its noun is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنَ الْمُصَلِّينَ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of نك; the verbal clause is the object of the saying (maqūl al-qawl). ﴿وَلَمْ نَكُ﴾ conjoined (maʿṭūf) to the preceding one; and ﴿نُطْعِمُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; and ﴿الْمِسْكِينَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi (direct object); the clause «نطعم..» is the khabar of نك. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ a defective past verb, and nā is its noun; and ﴿نَخُوضُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of كنا, and the clause «كنا..» is conjoined to what precedes it; and ﴿مَعَ﴾ an adverb of place, annexed to ﴿الْخائِضِينَ﴾. ﴿وَكُنَّا﴾ conjoined to the preceding one; and ﴿نُكَذِّبُ﴾ an imperfect verb whose fāʿil is latent; the clause is the khabar of كنا; and ﴿بِيَوْمِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the verb. ﴿الدِّينِ﴾ muḍāf ilayhi (genitive construct); and ﴿حَتَّى﴾ a particle of limit and a preposition; and ﴿أَتانَا﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿الْيَقِينُ﴾ its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from the implied an and the verb is in the position of a genitive (majrūr) by ḥattā, and the preposition with its genitive noun is attached to نكذب.

daas-irab:48-51.t: ﴿فَما﴾ the fāʾ is a resumptive particle; and ﴿ما﴾ negative; and ﴿تَنْفَعُهُمْ﴾ an imperfect verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿شَفاعَةُ﴾ fāʿil (agent), annexed to ﴿الشَّافِعِينَ﴾; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position. ﴿فَما﴾ an interrogative noun as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿لَهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ; the nominal clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the ḥāl (circumstantial). ﴿مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ ḥāl; and ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ﴾ kaʾanna, its noun and its predicate. ﴿مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ an adjective (ṣifa); the clause is a ḥāl. ﴿فَرَّتْ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil is latent (mustatir); and ﴿مِنْ قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to the verb; the clause is a second adjective of حمر.

daas-irab:52-53.t: ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression (iḍrāb); and ﴿يُرِيدُ كُلُّ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil (agent), annexed to ﴿امْرِئٍ﴾; and ﴿مِنْهُمْ﴾ a preposition and its genitive noun, attached to (mutaʿalliq) an omitted adjective (ṣifa) of امرئ; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿أَنْ يُؤْتى﴾ a passive imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the nāʾib fāʿil (deputy agent) is latent (mustatir); and ﴿صُحُفاً﴾ second mafʿūl bihi (direct object); and ﴿مُنَشَّرَةً﴾ an adjective of صحفا; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is mafʿūl bihi; and ﴿كَلَّا﴾ a particle of rebuke and deterrence (radʿ wa-zajr); and ﴿بَلْ﴾ a particle of digression; and ﴿لا﴾ negative; and ﴿يَخافُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb in the nominative (marfūʿ), and the wāw is its fāʿil; and ﴿الْآخِرَةَ﴾ mafʿūl bihi; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position.

daas-irab:54-56.t: ﴿كَلَّا﴾ an emphasis (tawkīd) of what precedes it; and ﴿إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾ and its noun and its predicate [Translator's note: so in the source; «inna» is evidently dropped: inna, its noun and its predicate]; the clause is initial (ibtidāʾiyya), with no grammatical position; and ﴿فَمَنْ﴾ the fāʾ is a conjunction; and ﴿من﴾ a conditional noun that makes jussive, as mubtadaʾ (subject); and ﴿شاءَ﴾ a past verb whose fāʿil (agent) is latent (mustatir), and it is the protasis (fiʿl al-sharṭ); and ﴿ذَكَرَهُ﴾ a past verb and its mafʿūl bihi (direct object), and the fāʿil is latent; the clause is the apodosis (jawāb al-sharṭ), with no grammatical position, and the two clauses of condition and apodosis are the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and the nominal clause is conjoined (maʿṭūf) to what precedes it. ﴿وَما﴾ negative; and ﴿يَذْكُرُونَ﴾ an imperfect verb and its fāʿil; the clause is resumptive, with no grammatical position; and ﴿إِلَّا﴾ a particle of exception; and ﴿أَنْ يَشاءَ اللَّهُ﴾ an imperfect verb in the accusative (manṣūb) by an, and the Name of Majesty is its fāʿil; the interpreted maṣdar formed from an and the verb is accusative by exception; and ﴿هُوَ أَهْلُ﴾ a mubtadaʾ and its khabar, annexed to ﴿التَّقْوى﴾; the nominal clause is causal (taʿlīl), with no grammatical position; and ﴿أَهْلُ الْمَغْفِرَةِ﴾ conjoined to what precedes it.

farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿يٰأَيُّهَا ٱلْمُدَّثِّرُ﴾.
He means: the one who has covered himself with his garments in order to sleep.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿ذَرْنِي وَمَنْ خَلَقْتُ وَحِيداً﴾.
There are two ways in [الوحيد]. Some said: leave Me [alone] with him whom I created by Myself alone. Others said: I created him alone, having neither wealth nor sons; and this is the more comprehensive of the two ways.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: goods, gold and silver. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] Muḥammad told us, he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from Ibrāhīm ibn al-Muhājir, from Mujāhid, concerning His saying: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مَالاً مَّمْدُوداً﴾; he said: a thousand dinars. We think that "extended" (mamdūd) was used for the number because a thousand is the limit of number: from a thousand one goes back to the beginning of counting. Similar to it is the Arabs' saying: لك على ألف أقدع (I owe you a full thousand), i.e. the limit of number.

farraa:13-13.t:
His saying: ﴿وَبَنِينَ شُهُوداً﴾.
He had ten sons who were never absent from his sight, either for trade or for work. And "the one alone" is al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra al-Makhzūmī.

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾.
They mention that he gathered the chiefs of the people of Mecca and said: The season [of pilgrimage] has drawn near, and the affair of this man has spread among the people; what will you say about him to the people? They said: We will say: [he is] mad. He said: Then people will come to him and speak with him, and he will be seen to be sane and sound, and they will call you liars. They said: We will say: a poet. He said: They are Arabs who have transmitted poems and know them, and Muḥammad's speech does not resemble poetry. They said: We will say: a soothsayer. He said: They know the soothsayers [112/b] and have questioned them, and they do not say: such and such will happen, if Allah wills; whereas Muḥammad tells you nothing without saying: if Allah wills. Then he stood up, and they said: al-Walīd has turned Sabian (ṣabaʾa) — meaning: al-Walīd has become Muslim. His nephew Abū Jahl said: I will deal with him for you. He went to him and said: Quraysh claim that you have turned Sabian, and they want to collect for you wealth that will suffice you in place of what you want to eat of the leftovers of Muḥammad's ﷺ companions. He said: Woe to you! By Allah, they never have their fill, so how would I seek their leftovers when I am the wealthiest of Quraysh? But I have been thinking about the affair of Muḥammad ﷺ, and what we should answer the Arabs when they ask us; and I have resolved to say: a sorcerer. This is the interpretation of His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وَقَدَّرَ﴾: [he reflected and determined] what to say about Muḥammad ﷺ.

farraa:19-19.t:
His saying: ﴿فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾.
قُتل, that is: he was cursed. Likewise ﴿قاتلهم الله﴾ and ﴿قُتِلَ الإِنْسَانُ ما أَكْفَرَهُ﴾: it is mentioned that these [mean] cursing.

farraa:2-2.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ﴾.
He means: arise and pray, and command [others] to pray.

farraa:21-22.t:
His saying: ﴿ثُمَّ نَظَرَ ثُمَّ عَبَسَ وَبَسَرَ﴾.
They mention that he passed by a group of Muslims in the Sacred Mosque, and they said: Will you come to Islam, O Abū al-Mughīra? He said: Your companion is nothing but a sorcerer, and his speech is nothing but sorcery that he learned from Musaylima the Liar and from the sorcerers of Babylon. Then — He said — he turned away from them in arrogance, having frowned and scowled: he grimaced, too proud to believe.

farraa:24-24.t: That is His saying: ﴿إِنْ هَذَآ إِلاَّ سِحْرٌ يُؤْثَرُ﴾: he transmits it from the people of Babylon.

farraa:26-26.t:
Allah, Majestic and Mighty, said: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾.
It is one of the names of Hell; for that reason it is not made fully declinable (lam yujra), and likewise "لظى".

farraa:29-29.t:
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It is joined back to سقر with the intention of repetition, as He said: ﴿ذُو الْعَرْشِ الْمَجِيدُ فَعَّالٌ لِمَا يُرِيدُ﴾, and as He said in the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: ﴿وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً﴾. Had it been "لواحةً للبشر" [in the accusative], it would be correct,
as He said: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ(35) نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾ (36). In the reading of Ubayy: "نذِيرٌ لِلْبشَر"; and all are correct.
[Translator's note: «وَهَذَا بَعْلِى شَيْخاً» is as printed; this is the standard reading, and the reading of ʿAbd Allāh usually cited at this point is «شيخٌ».]
His saying: ﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
It blackens the skin (al-bashara) by burning it.

farraa:30-31.t:
His saying: ﴿عَلَيْهَا تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾.
The Arabs give fatḥa to [the numbers] from أحد عشر to تسعة عشر in the genitive and the nominative [alike]. Some of them lighten the ʿayn in تسعة عشر, giving the ʿayn sukūn in the masculine; but they do not lighten it in ثلاث عشرة to تسع عشرة, because they only lightened [it] in the masculine because of the large number of vowels. As for the feminine, the shīn of عشْرة has sukūn, so they did not lighten its ʿayn, lest two quiescent letters meet. Likewise اثنا عشر in the masculine: the ʿayn is not lightened, because the alif of اثنا عشر is quiescent, so another letter is not given sukūn after it, lest two quiescent letters meet.
[Translator's note: «خفضوا» ("put in the genitive") is as printed; in context it means «خففوا» ("lightened").]
One of the unbelievers of the people of Mecca, namely Abū Jahl, said: And what are nineteen? A man among us can overpower one and keep him off the people. And a man of Banū Jumaḥ, whose kunya was Abū al-Ashaddayn, said: I will take care of seventeen for you; you take care of two for me. So Allah sent down: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَآ أَصْحَابَ ٱلنَّارِ إِلاَّ مَلاَئِكَةً﴾, i.e.: and who can overpower the angels? Then He said: ﴿وَمَا جَعَلْنَا عِدَّتَهُمْ ﴾ in its smallness ﴿إِلاَّ فِتْنَةً﴾ for those who disbelieve, so that they would say what they said. Then He said: ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُوتُواْ ٱلْكِتَابَ﴾: certainty added to their certainty, because the number of the keepers of Hell in their Book is nineteen; ﴿وَيَزْدَادَ ٱلَّذِينَ آمَنُوۤاْ إِيمَاناً﴾ because it is likewise in the Book of the People of the Book.

farraa:33-33.t:
His saying: ﴿وَٱللَّيْلِ إِذْ أَدْبَرَ﴾.
Ibn ʿAbbās read it: "والليل إذَا دَبر", and Mujāhid and some of the people of Medina likewise; and many people read it: "واللَّيْل إذْ أَدْبَر". [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Muḥammad ibn al-Faḍl told me that, from ʿAṭāʾ, from Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān, from Zayd, that he read it: "والليل إذْ أَدْبَر". In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh it is: "والليل إذا أدبر", and al-Ḥasan read it likewise: "إذا أدبر", as ʿAbd Allāh did.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told me, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from a man — I know him only as al-Agharr — from Ibn ʿAbbās, that he read: "والليل إذا دَبَر".
And he said: أدبر is only [said of] the back of a camel [i.e. being galled]. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us,] he said: al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and Qays told us, from ʿAlī ibn al-Aqmar, from Abū ʿAṭiyya, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Masʿūd, that he read "أدبر". [Al-Farrāʾ said: I think Abū ʿAṭiyya can only be al-Wādiʿī — indeed it is he. And al-Farrāʾ said: there is no إذ in Qays's report, and I consider the two only as two dialect forms.] One says: دبر النساء (sic), and the winter and the summer أدبر (went away); and likewise قَبَل and أقبل. But when they say: أقبل الراكب وأدبر (the rider came and went), they say it only with alif. To me the two are one in meaning; I do not rule out that what occurs with time-periods may occur with men.
[Translator's note: «دبر النساء» is as printed; «الشتاء» ("winter") or similar appears to be intended.]

farraa:35-35.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهَا لإِحْدَى ٱلْكُبَرِ﴾.
The هاء is a pronoun standing for Hell.

farraa:36-36.t:
His saying: ﴿نَذِيراً لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾.
One of the grammarians used to say: "نذيراً" is accusative [by] the beginning of the sura: O Muḥammad, arise as a warner to mankind. That is nothing, and Allah knows best, because much speech has come in between them, and its nominative in the reading of Ubayy rules out this meaning. Its accusative [rather] comes from His saying: ﴿إِنَّها لإحدى الكُبر نذيراً﴾: you detach it (taqṭaʿuhu) from the definite, because "إحدى الكبر" is definite, so you detached it from it [making it a ḥāl (circumstantial)]. Its accusative may also be by making النذير mean "warning", from His saying: ﴿لاَ تُبْقِى وَلاَ تَذَرُ﴾ لواحة [— you tell this about Hell as a warning] to mankind; for نذير may have the meaning of إنذار (warning). Allah, Blessed and Exalted, said: ﴿كَيْفَ نَذِير﴾ and ﴿فَكَيْفَ كان نكِير﴾, meaning: My warning and My reproach.

farraa:39-42.t:
His saying: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾.
Al-Kalbī said: they are the people of Paradise. [Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: and al-Fuḍayl ibn ʿIyāḍ told me, from Manṣūr ibn al-Muʿtamir, from al-Minhāl, tracing it back to ʿAlī, who said: ﴿إِلاَّ أَصْحَابَ ٱلْيَمِينِ﴾ — he said: they are the children. This seems right, because the children have not earned anything for which they would be held in pledge; and in His saying: ﴿يَتَسَآءَلُونَ عَنِ ٱلْمُجْرِمِينَ مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾ there is what strengthens [the view] that they are the children, because they did not know sins, so they asked: ﴿مَا سَلَكَكُمْ فِي سَقَرَ﴾.

farraa:4-4.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَثِيَابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾.
He is saying: do not be treacherous and so defile your garments, for the treacherous man is "soiled of garments". It is also said: "and purify your garments" [means] and set right your deeds. Some said: "and purify your garments" means: shorten them, for shortening garments is purification.

farraa:5-5.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلرُّجْزَ فَٱهْجُرْ﴾.
ʿĀṣim, al-Aʿmash and al-Ḥasan read it with kasra [الرِّجز], and al-Sulamī, Mujāhid and the people of Medina read it with ḍamma, reading: "والرجزُ فاهجر". Mujāhid explained: الرجز means the idols; and al-Kalbī explained it: الرجز is the punishment. We think that they are two dialect forms and that the meaning in both [112/a] is one.
[Translator's note: the source writes «والرجزُ» with a ḍamma on the zāy, while the point under discussion is the vowel of the rāʾ (الرُّجز).]

farraa:50-50.t:
His saying: ﴿كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾.
ʿĀṣim and al-Aʿmash read it: "مستنفِرة" with kasra, and the people of the Hijaz read it: "مستنفَرة" with fatḥa on the fāʾ; both are frequent in the speech of the Arabs. The poet said:
أمْسِكْ حِمارَكَ إِنَّهُ مُسْتنفِرٌ * فى إِثرِ أحْمِرَةٍ عَمْدنَ لِغُرّبِ
(Hold back your donkey, for it is bolting after she-asses that have made for Ghurrab.)
As for القسورة, it is said that it is the archers; and al-Kalbī said, with his chain of transmission: it is the lion.
[Abū al-ʿAbbās told us, he said: Muḥammad told us, he said:] al-Farrāʾ told us, he said: Abū al-Aḥwaṣ told me, from Saʿīd ibn Masrūq, [father of] Abū Sufyān al-Thawrī, from ʿIkrima, who said: It was said to him: القسورة is the lion in the language of the Abyssinians. He said: القسورة are the archers; the lion in the language of the Abyssinians is ʿanbasa.

farraa:52-52.t:
His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.
The unbelievers of Quraysh said to the Prophet ﷺ [114/a]: When a man among the Children of Israel committed a sin, his sin would be found written on a sheet in the morning; so why do we not see that? So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ ٱمْرِىءٍ مِّنْهُمْ أَن يُؤْتَىٰ صُحُفاً مُّنَشَّرَةً﴾.

farraa:54-54.t:
His saying: ﴿إِنَّهُ تَذْكِرَةٌ﴾.
He means this Qur'an. Had it been said: "إنها تذكرةٌ", it would be correct, as He said in [Sūrat] ʿAbasa. Whoever says (إنها) means the sura, and whoever says (إنه) means the Qur'an.

farraa:6-6.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلاَ تَمْنُن تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾.
He is saying: do not give anything in this world in order to receive more than it. In the reading of ʿAbd Allāh: "ولا تَمْنُن أنْ تَسْتَكْثِرَ", and this is evidence for the indicative (rafʿ) in "تستكثر". Had it been made jussive with this meaning, it would be correct; but the indicative is the way of the reading and of practice.

farraa:8-8.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَإِذَا نُقِرَ فِي ٱلنَّاقُورِ﴾.
It is said that it is the first of the two blasts.

zajjaj:1-1.t:
Sūrat al-Muddaththir
Meccan
﷽
His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿يا أيُّها المُدَّثِّرُ﴾ ("O you covered in a cloak"): the reading is with a doubled letter (tashdīd), the original being «المُتَدَثِّر»; the reason for it is like the reason in «المُتَزَمِّل», and its explanation is like the explanation of «المُزَّمِّل». It has also been narrated as «المُتَدَثِّر» with the tāʾ.

zajjaj:11-11.t: His saying: ﴿ذَرْنِي ومَن خَلَقْتُ وحِيدًا﴾ ("Leave Me with the one I created alone"): we have explained the meaning of ﴿ذَرْنِي﴾ in [Sūrat] al-Muzzammil. ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is on two lines. One is that «وَحِيدًا» describes Allah, Mighty and Majestic; the meaning is: "Leave Me with the one I created by Myself alone; no one shared with Me in creating him." Or ﴿وَحِيدًا﴾ describes the one created, and the meaning is: "Leave Me with the one I created alone, having neither wealth nor child."

zajjaj:12-13.t: ﴿وَجَعَلْتُ لَهُ مالا مَمْدُودًا﴾ ﴿وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا﴾ ("And to whom I granted extensive wealth, and sons present [with him]"): its implied sense is "wealth not cut off from him"; and it was said: "a thousand dinars". «وَبَنِينَ شُهُودًا», i.e. present with him, not needing to go about [for a livelihood] and be absent from him. It was said that by this al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra is meant; he had ten sons and was wealthy.

zajjaj:17-17.t: His saying: ﴿سَأُرْهِقُهُ صَعُودًا﴾ ("I will burden him with an arduous ascent"), i.e. I will lay upon him a hardship of punishment.

zajjaj:18-19.t:
His saying: ﴿إنَّهُ فَكَّرَ وقَدَّرَ﴾ ﴿فَقُتِلَ كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ ("Indeed, he thought and deliberated. So may he be destroyed how he deliberated!"): the meaning of «قُتِلَ» here is "may he be cursed", and similar to it is ﴿قُتِلَ الخَرّاصُونَ﴾ [al-Dhāriyāt: 10] ("Cursed be the liars").
Al-Walīd ibn al-Mughīra had said to the chiefs of the people of Mecca: "You have seen this man" — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — "and you know how his affair has spread. If people ask you about him, what will you say?" They said: "We shall say he is mad." He said: "Then they will speak with him and know that he is not mad." They said: "Then we shall say he is a poet." He said: "They are Arabs; they know poetry, and they know that what he has brought is not poetry." They said: "Then we shall say he is a soothsayer." He said: "Soothsayers do not say 'such-and-such will happen, if Allah wills', and he says 'if Allah wills'." So they said: "Al-Walīd has abandoned his religion (ṣabaʾa)." Abū Jahl, his brother's son, came and said: "The people are saying that you have abandoned your religion, and they have resolved to collect money for you as compensation for what you might be able to take from Muḥammad's companions." He said: "By Allah, they do not [even] eat their fill, so how could I take money from them, when I am among the wealthiest of people?" A group passed by him and mentioned to him what the Prophet ﷺ had brought, and he thought, and his face frowned and scowled (basara), i.e. he looked with intense displeasure, and he said: "This that Muḥammad has brought is nothing but magic he transmits from Musaylima and from the people of Babylon."

zajjaj:25-25.t: ﴿إنْ هَذا إلا قَوْلُ البَشَرِ﴾ ("This is not but the word of a human being"), i.e. this is nothing but the word of a human being.

zajjaj:26-26.t: ﴿سَأُصْلِيهِ سَقَرَ﴾ ("I will drive him into Saqar"): «سَقَرَ» is a diptote (does not take nunation), because it is definite and feminine; «سَقَر» is one of the names of Hell. Then Allah the Exalted made known the standing of Saqar in punishment, saying: ﴿وَما أدْراكَ ما سَقَرُ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 27] ("And what will make you know what Saqar is?"), whose interpretation is: "What has made you know what thing Saqar is?" Then He said: ﴿لا تُبْقِي ولا تَذَرُ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 28] ﴿لَوّاحَةٌ لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 29] ("It spares not and leaves not, scorching the skins"): «البَشَر» is the plural of «بَشَرَة» (skin), i.e. it burns the skin until it turns black.

zajjaj:3-3.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ﴾ ("And your Lord magnify"), i.e. describe Him with magnification and that He is the Greatest. The fāʾ came in on the sense of the answer of a condition (jawāb al-jazāʾ); the meaning is: «قُمْ فَأنْذِرْ» ("Arise and warn"), i.e. "arise and magnify your Lord."

zajjaj:30-30.t: ﴿عَلَيْها تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ﴾ ("Over it are nineteen"), i.e. over Saqar are nineteen angels; Allah described them in another place, saying: ﴿عَلَيْها مَلائِكَةٌ غِلاظٌ شِدادٌ لا يَعْصُونَ اللَّهَ ما أمَرَهم ويَفْعَلُونَ ما يُؤْمَرُونَ﴾ [al-Taḥrīm: 6] ("over which are angels, harsh and severe, who do not disobey Allah in what He commands them but do what they are commanded"). What the Basrans report is «تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ» with fatḥa on the ʿayn of «عَشَرَ». It has also been read with sukūn on the ʿayn, but the reading is with fatḥa. Whoever made it quiescent did so only because of the many vowels in succession; that is because they are two nouns made into a single noun, and for that reason both are indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa. Some read «تِسْعَةُ عَشَرَ», so it was inflected according to the original; that is rare in grammar, and the best is «تِسْعَةَ عَشَرَ», indeclinable on fatḥa. There is another variant in it: «تِسْعَةُ أعْشُرٍ», which is anomalous (shādhdh), as if on the plural of faʿīl as afʿul, like «يَمِين» and «أيْمُن».

zajjaj:31-31.t:
His saying, the Exalted: ﴿وَما جَعَلْنا عِدَّتَهم إلا فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ ("And We have not made their number except as a trial for those who disbelieve"), i.e. a test, because one of them said: "Some of us will be enough for these."
And His saying: ﴿لِيَسْتَيْقِنَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ﴾ ("so that those who were given the Scripture may be certain"), i.e. they know that what the Prophet (peace be upon him) brought agrees with what is in their scriptures; ﴿وَيَزْدادَ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إيمانًا﴾ ("and those who believe may increase in faith"), because whenever they affirm what comes in the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, their faith increases; ﴿وَلا يَرْتابَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الكِتابَ والمُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ ("and those who were given the Scripture and the believers may not doubt"), i.e. so that they do not doubt.
And His saying: ﴿وَما هي إلا ذِكْرى لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ ("And it is not but a reminder to humanity"): it has come in the exegesis that the fire in this world is a reminder of the Fire in the Hereafter.

zajjaj:33-33.t: His saying: ﴿واللَّيْلِ إذْ أدْبَرَ﴾ ("And by the night when it departs"); it is also read «إذا دَبَرَ», and both are good in Arabic: one says «دَبَرَ اللَّيْلُ» and «أدْبَرَ», and likewise «قَبَلَ اللَّيْلُ» and «أقْبَلَ». It has also been read «إذا أدْبَرَ والصُّبْحِ إذا أسْفَرَ» ("when it departs, and by the dawn when it brightens"), with the alif retained in both.

zajjaj:35-36.t: His saying: ﴿إنَّها لإحْدى الكُبَرِ﴾ ﴿نَذِيرًا لِلْبَشَرِ﴾ ("Indeed, it is one of the greatest [afflictions], as a warning to humanity"): this hāʾ is a pronoun referring to the Fire, i.e. it is great in its state of warning. The accusative of «نَذِيرًا» is as a ḥāl (circumstantial). «نَذِيرًا» is masculine because its meaning is the meaning of punishment; and the masculine may be on [the model of] their saying «اِمْرَأةٌ طاهِرٌ» and «طالِقٌ», i.e. "possessed of divorce"; likewise «نَذِيرًا» is "possessed of warning". It is also possible that «نَذِيرًا» is accusative, attached to (mutaʿalliq) the beginning of the sura, in the sense: "Arise as a warner to humanity."

zajjaj:37-37.t: His saying: ﴿لِمَن شاءَ مِنكم أنْ يَتَقَدَّمَ أوْ يَتَأخَّرَ﴾ ("to whoever among you wills to advance or hold back"), i.e. to advance in what he has been commanded, or to hold back — for you have been warned.

zajjaj:38-39.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿كُلُّ نَفْسٍ بِما كَسَبَتْ رَهِينَةٌ﴾ ﴿إلا أصْحابَ اليَمِينِ﴾ ("Every soul, for what it has earned, is held in pledge — except the companions of the right"). It was said: the companions of the right are the children, because they are not questioned; Allah has favoured them by giving them Paradise. Every soul is held in pledge for its deeds: they either free it or ruin it, and the freeing, along with its deeds, is by Allah's favour.

zajjaj:4-4.t:
﴿وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ ("And your garments purify") is like it [in structure]. The interpretation of ﴿وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ is: "Do not be treacherous" — the treacherous man is called «دَنِسُ الثِّيابِ» ("soiled of garments"). And ﴿وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ may mean: "your self purify". And it was said that ﴿وَثِيابَكَ فَطَهِّرْ﴾ means: "your garments shorten", because shortening the garment keeps it further from impurity, and when it trails on the ground one cannot be sure that something will not touch it and make it impure.
«والرِّجْزَ فاهْجُرْ» ("and filth avoid"), with kasra on the rāʾ, and it was also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ; their meaning is one, and their interpretation is: "Avoid the worship of idols." «الرِّجْز» in the language is punishment; Allah the Exalted said: ﴿وَلَمّا وقَعَ عَلَيْهِمُ الرِّجْزُ﴾ [al-Aʿrāf: 134] ("And when the punishment fell upon them"). So the interpretation on this basis is: "Whatever leads to Allah's punishment, avoid it."

zajjaj:45-45.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿وَكُنّا نَخُوضُ مَعَ الخائِضِينَ﴾ ("and we used to indulge with those who indulged"), i.e. we followed those who went astray.

zajjaj:48-48.t: His saying: ﴿فَما تَنْفَعُهم شَفاعَةُ الشّافِعِينَ﴾ ("So the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them"): He means the unbelievers. In this there is evidence that the believers are benefited by the intercession of one another.

zajjaj:49-49.t: His saying: ﴿فَما لَهم عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ ("Then what is the matter with them, turning away from the reminder?"): [«مُعْرِضِينَ»] is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial).

zajjaj:50-50.t:
﴿كَأنَّهم حُمُرٌ مُسْتَنْفِرَةٌ﴾ ("as if they were alarmed donkeys"); it was also read «مُسْتَنْفَرَةٌ» ("put to flight"). The poet said:
؎أمْسِكْ حِمارَكَ إنَّهُ مُسْتَنْفِرُ ∗∗∗ في إثْرِ أحْمِرَةٍ عَمَدْنَ لِغُرَّبِ
(Hold back your donkey, for he is bolting after she-asses that have made for Ghurrab.)

zajjaj:51-51.t: His saying: ﴿فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾ ("fleeing from a qaswara"): «القَسْوَرَة» is the lion; it was also said that «القَسْوَرَة» are the archers who hunt them.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿بَلْ يُرِيدُ كُلُّ امْرِئٍ مِنهم أنْ يُؤْتى صُحُفًا مُنَشَّرَةً﴾ ("Rather, every one of them desires to be given scrolls spread out"). It was said that they used to say: "Whoever of the Children of Israel committed a sin would find his sin written on his door the next day; so why are we not like that?" The explanation of their demand has come in the Qur'an in the Sura of "the Children of Israel", in His saying: ﴿وَلَنْ نُؤْمِنَ لِرُقِيِّكَ حَتّى تُنَـزِّلَ عَلَيْنا كِتابًا نَقْرَؤُهُ﴾ [al-Isrāʾ: 93] ("And we will not believe in your ascension until you bring down to us a book we may read").

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying: ﴿هُوَ أهْلُ التَّقْوى وأهْلُ المَغْفِرَةِ﴾ ("He is worthy of being feared and worthy to forgive"), i.e. He is worthy that His punishment be guarded against, and worthy that what leads to His forgiveness be acted upon.

zajjaj:6-6.t: ﴿وَلا تَمْنُنْ تَسْتَكْثِرُ﴾ ("And do not confer favour seeking more"), i.e. do not give anything intending to take in return something greater than it. «تَسْتَكْثِرُ» is an anticipated ḥāl (circumstantial; ḥāl mutawaqqaʿa). This is specifically for the Prophet ﷺ; there is no sin on a person in giving a gift through which he hopes for something greater than it, but Allah trained the Prophet ﷺ in the noblest manners and the most exalted character.

zajjaj:8-9.t: His saying: ﴿فَإذا نُقِرَ في النّاقُورِ﴾ ﴿فَذَلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ﴾ ("And when the horn is sounded, that Day will be a difficult day"): «النّاقُور» is the Trumpet, and it was said in the exegesis that He means by it the first blast. ﴿يَوْمٌ عَسِيرٌ﴾ is nominative by His saying ﴿فَذَلِكَ يَوْمَئِذٍ﴾ [i.e. as its khabar]; the meaning is: "That is a difficult day, the day the Trumpet is blown." «يَوْمَئِذٍ» may be nominative and may be accusative. If it is nominative, it was made indeclinable (mabnī) on fatḥa only because of its annexation to «إذْ», since «إذْ» is non-declinable (ghayr mutamakkina). If it is accusative, it is on the meaning: "That is a difficult day, on the day the Trumpet is blown."
